e.text: Asking for three distinct bets to fill opening weekend with young, sustainability-minded locals.

e.note: Designing 3 different bets

strategies.name: Media-led digital push
strategies.thesis: This crowd over-indexes on Rich Roll (0.93) and The Minimalists (0.92), and Airbnb is their top brand (0.95), so early host-read ads plus a full-run co-branded drop and early city-wide fit-weighted social build word of mouth across the city before opening weekend (sim: ~3,056 adopters, best of all tests).

e.text: A1 reaches 23.9% versus the benchmark's 6.1%; asking the Critic what could push it further.

e.note: Reading results for A1, A2, A3

critique.summary: A1's early podcasts, the full-run Airbnb collab and fit-weighted city social reach 23.9% (P10 22.6%) at $4.56 per adopter, nearly 4x the benchmark's 6.1%, with 57.7% of adoption from word of mouth. Local tactics underperform: $300 partners return 7–18 adopters, while late pop-ups and street teams (day 39–40) return 3–10 adopters for $450–$2500.

findings.finding: A1 has the best mean and the best floor (P10 22.6%) at $4.56 per adopter; the Airbnb collab (411 adopters for $2000) and the two podcasts (189 and 177 adopters) lead per dollar.
The SkyBar pop-up on day 40 earned 10 adopters for $2500 and the street teams 9 and 5, so Uniqlo/IKEA districts lift to 26.6% but overall reach falls to 18.3% at $5.89 per adopter.
A3's Headspace collab (317) trails Airbnb (411–429) at the same $2000, and the day-39 street:3 earned only 3 adopters, leaving the weakest plan at 16.3% reach and $6.69 per adopter.
Untargeted broad social yields 234 adopters for $7560, while targeted social yields 403–515, confirming that taste targeting roughly doubles social efficiency.

changes.change: Keep A1's core (both podcasts on days 2 and 8, the Airbnb collab for days 0–42, social:city) and extend social:city from 34 to 42 days.
changes.why: Social was the top driver in A2 and A3 when run for all 42 days, and the leftover budget covers part of the extension.

changes.change: Drop popup:9967C655 (day 40) and street:2, street:4 and street:3 in every variant.
changes.why: They returned 3–10 adopters for $450–$2500, and seeding on day 39–40 leaves no time for word of mouth to spread.

changes.change: If budget allows after trimming social days, add the two best partners on day 0: 6D5D521D/La Mojarra in zone 3 and the Nivel 40 SkyBar partner in zone 4.
changes.why: At about 16 adopters each for $300, these were the most efficient local actions, and zones 3–4 have high fit (0.59).

changes.change: Avoid zone 1 (Fuentes Brotantes, fit 0.248) and weak partners such as A-las Miches.
changes.why: Zone 1 has low fit, and A-las Miches returned only 7 adopters for $300.

Local tactics underperform: $300 partners return 7–18 adopters, while late pop-ups and street teams (day 39–40) return 3–10 adopters for $450–$2500.

e.text: A1 holds at 23.9% with a 22.6% floor; checking whether Benito Juárez and Coyoacán residents would actually show up.

e.note: Asking residents across the city

voices.name: Daniela
voices.quote: I saw an Instagram ad for it last week, and honestly it caught me because I already wear Patagonia for hiking around Los Dinamos. Roma Norte is a trek from here, but I'd go after tacos at Pacos if the shoes actually hold up on trails.
voices.change: Proof the soles survive real trail use, not just city walking.

voices.name: Andrés
voices.quote: Yeah, an ad popped up on my feed, something about sustainable sneakers. I like the idea, I'm a North Face and Patagonia guy, but I'd want to see if they're comfortable before I cross the city for them.
voices.change: Trying them on at a weekend event closer to the south.

voices.name: Valeria
voices.quote: I actually heard it on The Minimalists, which surprised me because I didn't expect a Mexico City shout-out there. Simple design, fewer things that last longer, that's kind of my Uniqlo logic, so I'll probably stop by before drinks at Seven Sins.
voices.change: Clean, minimal colorways and a fair price would make me bring friends.

voices.name: Kevin
voices.quote: Pues I think I scrolled past an ad but didn't really stop. I'm more into gaming and going to perreo nights, and Roma Norte is kind of far for shoes I don't know.
voices.change: A collab with a reggaeton artist or a game skin tie-in.

e.text: A1 is the most reliable plan: 23.9% reach, floor 22.6%, nearly four times the benchmark. Locking it in.

e.note: Writing the launch plan for A1

plan.headline: Roma Norte sustainable sneaker pop-up: projected ~3,270 adopters (23.9% of the natural audience, 22.6%–25.0% range) on $14,920. This is a Qloo-based simulation, not a guarantee.
plan.summary: We are betting on media this crowd already loves: host-read ads on The Rich Roll Podcast and The Minimalists, a full-run co-branded drop with Airbnb, and fit-weighted social ads across Mexico City starting six weeks out. Qloo taste data shows strong over-indexing on Rich Roll (0.93), The Minimalists (0.92) and Airbnb (0.95), with Patagonia and Veja fans as the pull. The simulation projects about 3,269 adopters at $4.56 each, with 57.7% of adoption coming from word of mouth. That is roughly 4x the 843 adopters projected for spending the same budget where the crowds are, but it remains a simulation, not a promise.

weeks.label: Week 1 (days 42–36 before launch)
items: Day 42: start the Airbnb co-branded drop ($2,000). It runs through launch.
Day 41: launch fit-weighted social ads across Mexico City ($6,120, running 34 days).
Day 39: run the host-read ad on The Rich Roll Podcast ($3,450).

weeks.label: Week 2 (days 35–29 before launch)
items: Day 33: run the host-read ad on The Minimalists ($3,350).
Shift social creative toward minimal colorways and fair price, which is the hook in the Minimalists listener's quote.

weeks.label: Weeks 3–5 (days 28–8 before launch)
items: Keep social running. Feature sole and trail-durability proof aimed at Patagonia and Veja fans.
Review the weekly metrics and rebalance social weighting toward districts that are lagging.

weeks.label: Final week and launch (days 7–0)
items: Social ads wrap up around day 7. The Airbnb drop carries through opening.
Opening weekend at Roma Norte: encourage people to bring friends, so the word of mouth the plan relies on has something to spread.

media.name: Host-read ad on The Rich Roll Podcast
media.action: Host-read ad on The Rich Roll Podcast, 39 days before launch, $3,450.
media.why: Qloo affinity 0.93. Draws Patagonia (41%) and Veja (35%) fans. Credited with 189 adopters.

media.name: Host-read ad on The Minimalists

media.why: Qloo affinity 0.92. Draws Veja (40%) and Patagonia (34%) fans. Credited with 177 adopters.

risks: These projections come from a simulation built on Qloo taste data. Real reach can and will differ.
South-side fans say Roma Norte is far to travel. Some want to try shoes on first or see proof the soles hold up on trails.
The Fortnite and reggaeton district (20.2%) and the Stranger Things, K-pop and Latin pop district (21.5%) lag the rest. Gaming and reggaeton fans show little pull.
Word of mouth drives 57.7% of projected adoption. If early adopters stay quiet, results drop sharply.
measure: Weekly visits and sign-ups attributed to each podcast's promo code and to the Airbnb drop.
